rows.name: Bracketed paste (DECSET 2004)
rows.requirement: App probe: query DECRPM for private mode 2004 with CSI ? 2004 $ p. Expected: set, reset or permanently set (Ps 1-3) is supported as mode recognition only; permanently reset (Ps 4) is unsupported, because the terminal knows the mode and cannot set it. Not recognized (Ps 0) is inconclusive, and no reply is PROBE INVALID. The DECRPM reply does not measure paste delimiters. Library arm: where no DECRPM reply comes, a controlled public state or effect read decides. App arm: where DECRPM gives no reply or Ps 0, a controlled effect read in the same run decides: the effect appears with the mode set and not with it reset. A missing reply alone decides nothing and stays PROBE INVALID when no effect read is made. Where the terminal answers no mode report, the row is decided by effect: the same input is sent with the mode off and on, and the app's received bytes decide.

rows.name: Viewport holds on output
rows.requirement: Library probe: observe a fresh numbered seed with exact retained history, qualify an inward viewport scroll at fixed extents, then emit one marker row without keyboard input. An unchanged anchor holds; a snap to the new bottom fails; partial drift or failed controls remain inconclusive. Verify return to bottom before reading the marker, and repeat independently with the exact synchronized-output bytes. Manual UI probe. Fill scrollback with at least two pages of lines, scroll the viewport up until the live bottom is no longer visible, then emit a uniquely named marker line without keyboard input. Pass if the viewport remains on the old lines; fail if it jumps to the marker at the bottom. Repeat with the marker wrapped in \x1b[?2026h ... \x1b[?2026l to check synchronized output, and record any terminal setting that changes the result. Automated Linux application probe (contexts with XTEST wheel and pixel capture): qualify the wheel-movement bound in the same run before the hold phases on a numbered seed with N + 1 history lines above the bottom, where N is the smaller of the row count and 12, by capturing the bottom frame, turning the wheel up one notch, turning it up N more notches to clamp at the seed top, verifying restoration to the bottom frame, and requiring the one-notch scrolled frame to differ by cell-aligned digest from the top-clamped scrolled frame (both scrolled, so rows per notch is between 1 and N; unmoved, over-bound or unchanging scrolled frames stay PROBE TODO), then clear and re-seed so calibration never touches the history under test. Record a fixed tail frame cropped to the seeded label columns before any hold-phase viewport input, then seed unique history lines with enough space for the measured wheel-movement bound. Scroll up and record the anchor. If the non-printing parse-witness query sent before the output returns the scrolled viewport to a frame equal to the bottom frame captured before scrolling up, the terminal does not hold its viewport on output and the result is Unsupported; any other movement by the witness stays PROBE TODO. Append unique output followed by the identical tail. After all bounded downward inputs, capture the bottom once and require an exact match to the original tail reference. Compare the output frame with the earlier anchor, that verified bottom and the same upward displacement from the new bottom; accept exactly one match. Restore to the tail reference again before independently repeating with synchronized output. Use cell-aligned label-column digests from calibrated same-run pixel captures, without pixel masks. An unknown or ambiguous movement bound, failed control, unproved restoration or ambiguous match keeps PROBE TODO; capture or harness errors are PROBE INVALID. Multiplexers (tmux and GNU Screen) and other application contexts without XTEST wheel scroll and pixel capture keep the existing manual recipe and named PROBE TODO.

rows.name: Current directory (OSC 7)
rows.requirement: Headless: retain the original URI. Set a distinct OSC 633 ; P ; Cwd=... BEL control and read it through the same getCwd reader before sending two distinct OSC 7 ; file://localhost/... BEL target URIs. Supported requires both target values to equal the expected URLs after WHATWG URL serialization; the raw values are retained. A failed target is Unsupported only when the control URI was observed; without that control it is PROBE TODO. Restore the original URI with OSC 7, falling back to OSC 633 P Cwd if needed. A restoration mismatch is PROBE INVALID, never Unsupported. Retain original, control, target and restored readings. Applications report PROBE TODO unless the terminal shows the path on a public surface. Where it does, a control proves that surface reads back, each target is read from it, and a made-up OSC leaves it unchanged; the raw readings are retained.

rows.name: 24-bit truecolor
rows.requirement: Headless: send SGR 38;2;255;128;0 and SGR 38;2;17;97;201 (semicolon form) and require both foreground cells to match their requested RGB values exactly. A negative requires independent named-color controls that calibrate the channel; missing or colliding readback does not establish a negative. App: send SGR 38;2;255;128;0 (semicolon form), compare with neutral and nearest-palette-color controls, and require repeated target paint to agree; capture differences do not establish the exact rendered RGB. DECRQSS and cursor advance alone do not verify the painted color.

rows.name: Mode 2031 color scheme reporting
rows.requirement: Library mode-state criterion: DECSET private mode 2031, query DECRPM and read getMode, then DECRST, query and read again. Supported requires Ps 1 after set, Ps 2 after reset and getMode true then false. Ps 0, 2 or 4 after DECSET is Unsupported. No reply stays review PROBE TODO; null or disagreeing getMode and every other reply pair, including Ps 3, stay PROBE TODO. scheme-change report (CSI ? 997 ; Ps n, unsolicited) unmeasured; recognition measured. App protocol criterion: snapshot DECRPM mode 2031. Ps 1 or 3 is Supported without mutation; Ps 0 or 4 is Unsupported without mutation. Ps 2 sends DECSET, queries again, then restores DECRST: Ps 1 or 3 is Supported; still Ps 2 is Unsupported (recognized but DECSET refused (mode kept reset)). No reply is PROBE TODO: no DECRPM reply. Requires existing disposable-terminal authority. presentation (tearing, scroll cadence, inverted frame) unmeasured; protocol measured

rows.name: OSC 52 clipboard write
rows.requirement: In an isolated headless backend with clipboard-state readback, write a known OSC 52 c control and confirm that exact selector and encoded payload in the same clipboard witness. Write a fresh distinct probe nonce and require its exact selector and encoded payload as a new retained write. If the control is not recorded, report PROBE TODO because no same-path control was observed. If the control is recorded but the probe write is missing, report PROBE TODO: control OSC 52 c write recorded but the probe write was not; same-run observations disagree. A different retained write is inconclusive. A headless backend without a clipboard witness writes a fresh nonce and reads it back through a complete OSC 52 reply. In an owned disposable Linux display, a real key event precedes the write, as on any used terminal; then write a fresh OSC 52 nonce and check the clipboard independently with X11, then restore and verify the baseline. Without the owned fixture, live collection sends no clipboard traffic; the site displays PROBE TODO because no clipboard operation is attempted.

observed.reason: The independent GTK peer read the exact nonce from the App-owned X11 CLIPBOARD.

rows.name: System clipboard paste
rows.requirement: App probe: after a control keypress proves keys reach the terminal, seed an owned nonce into the selection the terminal's default paste action reads, and press that action's key with mode 2004 off, then on, then off. Supported: the on paste arrives as CSI 200~nonce CSI 201~ and both off pastes arrive as the raw nonce. Unsupported: the on paste arrives raw. Anything else fails the reply. The owned selection and the incoming 2004 mode are restored and verified; a failed restore fails the run. The selection and key used are in each row's evidence. Library probe: the engine's native paste runs twice with 2004 off and twice with it on; Supported when the off pastes arrive raw and the on pastes arrive bracketed, Unsupported when the on pastes arrive raw, with the incoming 2004 mode restored and verified.
rows.blocker: No retained default OS paste action with an independently seeded owned selection, delivery control and off/on/off byte comparisons satisfies this current application criterion.
